title: Predict
bodyMarkdown: The editor has three lines of code in it. Read them. **Do not run them yet.**

question.prompt: What will the second line show on the screen?

options.feedback: Yes. The comma puts a space between the two pieces of text.
Close. Look at what the comma does when you run it.
The quotes and the comma are instructions to Python. They do not appear on the screen.

title: Run
bodyMarkdown: Press **Run** and look at the console. Were you right?

title: Investigate
bodyMarkdown: Look at the first line of the program again.

question.prompt: Which word tells Python to show something on the screen?
question.feedbackWrong: It is the word at the very start of each line, just before the first bracket.

title: Modify
bodyMarkdown: Change the program so that it greets **you** instead of the world, and uses your name instead of Pip.

question.prompt: Change the first two lines, then press Check.

title: Make
bodyMarkdown:
Clear the editor and write a program of your own.

- Print at least three lines.
- On one of the lines, print two or more things with a comma between them.

question.prompt: Write your three lines, then press Check.
